headline: NCP leader Mahmuda threatened again, told to leave country if she cares about her family

members.title: Attempt made to harass Nahid Islam at Cambridge University campus
members.lead: A group of activists and supporters of the Awami League, whose activities are banned in Bangladesh, attempted to harass Nahid Islam, convener of the National Citizen Party (NCP), on the campus of the University of Cambridge in the United Kingdom. However, they failed to do so due to the intervention of NCP activists in the UK. Nahid Islam, chief whip of the opposition in parliament and one of the key figures behind the July mass uprising that toppled the Awami League government, is currently visiting the UK on a week-long trip. He attended an exchange of views organised by the Cambridge University Bangla Society at the main lecture theatre of the Old Divinity School at St John's College, University of Cambridge, on Saturday evening (local time). After the event, as Nahid was getting into a car to leave the venue, he came face to face with a group of Awami League supporters who had gathered there beforehand. . Mohammad MA Himel, immediate past member secretary of the NCP UK Alliance, was present at the scene. Around midnight Bangladesh time, he posted a video of the incident on his verified Facebook account. The video shows several expatriate Bangladeshis supporting the NCP helping Nahid into a car. Meanwhile, another group of NCP supporters were engaged in a heated exchange with several Awami League supporters near the front of the vehicle. The car carrying Nahid left the scene amid the commotion. In the caption accompanying the video, Himel wrote: “This is how we exit Nahid Islam from the Cambridge University seminar. Awami League couldn't even touch us!” In another video posted by Himel, NCP supporters can be seen chanting slogans against the Awami League. . Its caption read: “NCP gives a crushing response to Awami League's goons in Cambridge.” Asked about the incident, Ehteshamul Haque, convener of the preparation committee for Nahid Islam's UK visit, told Prothom Alo today that the Awami League had repeatedly attempted to harass NCP leaders in the UK. “They trie…

members.title: NCP leader Mahmuda threatened again, told to leave country if she cares about her family
members.lead: Mahmuda Alam Mitu, a Member of Parliament (MP) for the reserved women's seat nominated by the 11-party alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami and a leader of the National Citizen's Party (NCP), has been threatened again. On Sunday afternoon, while she was in the National Parliament, a phone call warned her, "If you care about your family, leave the country quickly. If not, you can stay; it’s not a problem." In the evening, a message from the NCP was sent to the media announcing the threat. The NCP also sent an audio recording of a 2 minute and 40-second conversation between MP Mahmuda and the young male caller to the media. .Banned Chhatra League threatened and abused me over phone: Samantha Sharmin . The message from the party stated, "The call came at 5:29 PM. At that time, Mahmuda Alam was in the National Parliament." In the recording, the supporter, affiliated with the Awami League, told NCP leader and doctor Mahmuda Alam, "You will be torn apart. So please, be careful. You must leave the country." At one point, the young Awami League supporter told Mahmuda, "If you care about your family, leave the country quickly. If not, you can stay; it’s not a problem." He ended the call by saying he would call again at the same time tomorrow, Monday. . Earlier, last Friday evening, Dr. Mahmuda Alam posted on her verified Facebook account about receiving threats. She wrote, "For the past seven days, I have been receiving death threats directly on the phone and WhatsApp. I received threats before, yet even if I report these, attempts might be made to downplay the issue like Nusrat's incident." Amid various activities of the banned Awami League surrounding the announcement of the return of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, ousted in the July mass uprising, by December, a total of three NCP members, including Mahmuda, have faced threats and attacks.
